analysis.text:
Strengths: Dybantsa has elite positional size, strength and movement skills, and he thrives attacking downhill and in the midrange. He excels at drawing fouls and playing through contact. He showed growth making decisions and plays for teammates this season.

Weaknesses: Dybantsa is inconsistent shooting from long range and needs to continue sharpening his handle, which will determine his offensive ceiling. He has great defensive upside but doesn't apply himself consistently on that end.

The verdict: Viewed as a potential No. 1 pick since his freshman year of high school, Dybantsa managed to exceed expectations at BYU leading D-I in scoring while shooting 51% and improving as the season went along. He reminded NBA teams of just how special his offensive tool kit is, with his trajectory comparing favorably to star wings Kawhi Leonard and Jaylen Brown. He looks the part as a franchise player, with time and room to expand his game on both ends of the floor. -- Jeremy Woo

Strengths: Peterson is the most gifted scorer in this draft. He is a remarkable long-range shotmaker capable of prolonged hot streaks, special qualities that give him major upside. He's a strong athlete with good size for a ball handler who also competes defensively.

Weaknesses: Peterson played on the ball plenty in high school, but he wasn't able to show much of that at Kansas due to personnel and style of play. Sharpening his handle and getting more playmaking reps will be key to realizing his ceiling.

The verdict: After entering the fall projected at No. 1, Peterson struggled to stay healthy and played through a strange season after a battle with cramping. His best moments underscored why teams view him as a future star -- he showed breathtaking flashes of his ceiling. When things are going well, he looks like the best shooter in the draft. He can become one of the NBA's top scorers in time, assuming a clean bill of health. NBA execs liken him stylistically to Devin Booker. -- Woo
